title: 青玉案·送伯固归吴中
title_en: Green Jade Table: Seeing Bogu Off Home to Wuzhong
author: 苏轼

text_note.zh: 原始资料只题词牌“青玉案”。通行本加题目“送伯固归吴中”。第五句原始资料作“莫惊鸥鹭”，通行本（如《宋词三百首》）作“莫惊鸳鹭”，这里从通行本。
text_note.en: The source gives only the tune name, Qingyu'an. Common editions add the title "Seeing Bogu Off Home to Wuzhong". In line 5 the source has "gulls and egrets"; common editions such as Three Hundred Song Lyrics have "mandarin ducks and egrets". The common text is used here.

readings.zh: “老子”是老人自称“我”，在诗词里读 lǎo zǐ。
readings.en: Lǎo zǐ is an old man calling himself "I"; in poetry it is read lǎo zǐ.

readings.zh: 这里是名词“地方”，读 chù。
readings.en: Here it is a noun, "place", so it is read chù.

readings.zh: 这里是“曾经”的意思，读 céng。
readings.en: Here it means "once, before", so it is read céng.

glosses.zh: 枕上：躺在枕头上，指睡梦里。
glosses.en: zhěn shàng: on the pillow, that is, in dreams.

glosses.zh: 吴中：今天江苏苏州一带。伯固要回那里去。
glosses.en: Wú zhōng: the area around today's Suzhou in Jiangsu, where Bogu was going home.

glosses.zh: 黄耳：晋朝陆机养的一条狗，名叫黄耳。传说它能替陆机在洛阳和吴地之间送信。
glosses.en: Huáng ěr: Yellow Ear, a dog kept by Lu Ji in the Jin dynasty. Legend says it carried his letters between Luoyang and his home in Wu.

glosses.zh: 松江：吴淞江，从太湖流出，经过吴中。
glosses.en: Sōng jiāng: the Wusong River, which flows out of Lake Tai past Wuzhong.

glosses.zh: 呼小渡：喊小渡船来摆渡。
glosses.en: hū xiǎo dù: to call for a small ferry boat.

glosses.zh: 鸳鹭：鸳鸯和白鹭，水边的鸟。
glosses.en: yuān lù: mandarin ducks and egrets, birds by the water.

glosses.zh: 四桥：吴江一带的桥，一说指第四桥。
glosses.en: sì qiáo: the bridges around Wujiang; one view is that it means one bridge known as the Fourth Bridge.

glosses.zh: 老子：老夫，我。苏轼自称，带点玩笑的口气。
glosses.en: lǎo zǐ: this old man, me. Su Shi calls himself this half in jest.
jīng xíng chù: places I have walked through.

glosses.zh: 辋川图：王维画的辋川风景图。辋川是王维隐居的地方。
glosses.en: Wǎng chuān tú: Wang Wei's painting of Wangchuan, the valley where he lived in retirement.

glosses.zh: 高人：品格高尚、不追名利的人。
glosses.en: gāo rén: a person of lofty character who does not chase fame.

glosses.zh: 右丞：王维，他做过尚书右丞这个官。
glosses.en: Yòu chéng: Wang Wei, who once held the post of Right Assistant Minister.

glosses.zh: 作个归期：定下一个回去的日子。
glosses.en: zuò gè guī qī: to set a date for going home.

glosses.zh: 天已许：老天已经答应了。
glosses.en: tiān yǐ xǔ: heaven has already agreed.
chūn shān: a light spring robe.

glosses.zh: 小蛮：本来是唐代白居易家里的歌女，这里借指苏轼家中的侍妾，一说指王朝云。
glosses.en: Xiǎo mán: first the name of a singing girl in the household of the Tang poet Bai Juyi. Here it stands for a woman of Su Shi's own household; one view is that it means Wang Zhaoyun.

glosses.zh: 西湖：杭州的西湖。苏轼在杭州做过官。
glosses.en: Xī hú: West Lake in Hangzhou, where Su Shi had served as an official.

translation.zh: 三年来，我在梦里常常走在回吴中的路上。
translation.en: For three years, in my dreams, I have walked the road to Wuzhong.
I wish I could send a dog like Yellow Ear

translation.zh: 你要是到了松江，喊小船来摆渡，
translation.en: If you reach the Song River and call for a little ferry,

translation.zh: 可别惊动了水边的鸳鸯和白鹭。
translation.en: do not startle the ducks and egrets.

translation.zh: 全是我当年走过的地方。
translation.en: every spot is a place I once walked.

translation.zh: 我在王维的辋川图上看暮春的景色，
translation.en: I gaze at late spring in Wang Wei's painting of Wangchuan,

translation.zh: 常常想起这位高人写的诗句。
translation.en: and often recall the lines of that lofty man.

translation.zh: 我定下了回去的日子，老天也已经答应了。
translation.en: I have set a date to go home, and heaven has agreed.

translation.zh: 还是家里人一针一线缝的，
translation.en: sewn stitch by stitch by someone dear,

translation.zh: 上面曾经沾湿过西湖的雨。
translation.en: was once wet with the rain of West Lake.

background.zh: 伯固是苏坚的字。苏轼在杭州做官时，苏坚是他手下的官员，两人交情很深。后来苏坚要回吴中（今天的苏州一带），苏轼写了这首词送他。苏轼自己也很喜欢吴中的山水，盼着有一天也能回去隐居。这首词一般认为写于苏轼第二次在杭州做官之后，具体年份说法不一。
background.en: Bogu was the courtesy name of Su Jian. When Su Shi was an official in Hangzhou, Su Jian worked under him, and the two became close friends. When Su Jian was going home to Wuzhong, the area around today's Suzhou, Su Shi wrote this lyric to see him off. Su Shi loved the scenery of Wuzhong too, and hoped one day to retire there. The lyric is usually dated after Su Shi's second term in Hangzhou, but the exact year is debated.

author_note.zh: 苏轼（1037—1101），号东坡居士，北宋大文学家。他两次在杭州做官，修过西湖的苏堤，对江南感情很深。他很佩服王维，说王维“诗中有画，画中有诗”。这首词里也提到王维的辋川图和诗句，表达他想退隐的心愿。
author_note.en: Su Shi (1037–1101), also called Dongpo, was a great Northern Song writer. He served in Hangzhou twice and built the Su Causeway across West Lake, so he loved the south deeply. He greatly admired Wang Wei, and said that in Wang Wei's poems there are paintings, and in his paintings there are poems. This lyric mentions Wang Wei's painting and verses to show his own wish to retire.

appreciation.zh: 这是一首送别词，却写得轻松亲切。开头说三年来做梦都在走吴中的路，真想派陆机的狗黄耳跟着朋友回去。接着像在叮嘱朋友：到了松江坐船，别吓着鸟儿，那些桥边都是“老子”走过的地方。一个“老子”，透出苏轼的幽默。下半首写自己：看着王维的画，想着王维的诗，已经和老天约好了回去的日子。最后落在一件春衫上：针线是家里人缝的，衣上还沾过西湖的雨。一件旧衣服，装着对家人、对朋友、对江南的全部怀念。
appreciation.en: This is a farewell lyric, yet it feels light and friendly. It begins: for three years I have walked the road to Wuzhong in my dreams, and I wish I could send Lu Ji's dog Yellow Ear home with you. Then it is like friendly advice: when you take a boat on the Song River, do not scare the birds, because every bridge there is a place this old man has walked. Calling himself "this old man" shows Su Shi's humor. The second half is about himself. He looks at Wang Wei's painting, thinks of Wang Wei's poems, and has already agreed with heaven on a day to go home. It ends on a spring robe. It was sewn by someone dear, and it once got wet in the rain of West Lake. One old robe holds all his longing for family, for his friend, and for the south.
